aarti.tek: This is the āratī of Kuñjabihārī, who roams the groves; of Śrī Giridhara Kṛṣṇa Murāri.
aarti.pad1: A Vaijayantī garland is round his neck; the boy plays his sweet flute. Earrings glitter in his ears; Nanda's darling son is Nanda's joy. The dark radiance of his limbs is like the sky; Rādhikā is shining, O friend. Vanamālī stands among the creepers. Curls like black bees, a tilaka of musk, a glow like the moon; and the beauty of dear Śyāmā is lovely. ॥1॥
aarti.pad2: The golden crown of peacock feathers shines; the gods long for a sight of him. Heaps of flowers rain down from the sky. The mouth harp sounds, and the sweet mṛdaṅga; the cowherd girls are with him; and the love of the cowherd maidens is matchless. ॥2॥
aarti.pad3: Where Gaṅgā came forth — Śrī Gaṅgā, who takes away the impurity of the Kali age, by remembering whom delusion is broken; who dwells on Śiva's head, amid his matted locks, and takes away the mire of sin — that is the beauty of Śrī Banavārī's feet. ॥3॥
aarti.pad4: The bright sand of the bank glitters; the flute is sounding in Vṛndāvana; on every side are gopīs, cowherds and cows. He smiles, softly and gently; the moon sheds its light; the snares of worldly existence are cut. Hear the call of a poor beggar. ॥4॥
